question.text: Two gases occupy two containers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>; the gas in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>, of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>, exerts a pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MPa</mi></math> and that in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>, of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>, exerts a pressure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MPa</mi></math>. The two containers are joined by a tube of negligible volume and the gases are allowed to intermingle. Then if the temperature remains constant, the final pressure in the containers will be (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>MPa</mi></math>)

solution.text:
As the quantity of gas remains constant μ A + μ B = μ

        PAVART+PBVBRT=PVA+VBRT

        P=PAVA+PBVBVA+VB=1.4×0.1+0.7×0.150.1+0.15

⇒   P=0.98 MPa
